'''Roald Zinnurovich Sagdeev''' ({{langx|ru|Роальд Зиннурович Сагдеев}}, {{langx|tt-Cyrl|Роальд Зиннур улы Сәгъдиев}}; born 26 December 1932) is a Russian expert in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and a former director of the [[Russian Space Research Institute|Space Research Institute of the USSR Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=bio>{{langx|ru|[http://www.1000kzn.ru/article/ru/1313/383/ Biography]}}</ref> He was also a science advisor to the Soviet President [[Mikhail Gorbachev]]. Sagdeev graduated from [[Moscow State University]]. He is a member of both the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Roald+Zinnurovich+Sagdeev&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-04-28|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> He has worked at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] since 1989 in the [[University of Maryland College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences]]. He is also currently a senior advisor at the [[Albright Stonebridge Group]], a global strategy firm, where he assists clients with issues involving Russia and countries of the former Soviet Union. Sagdeev was married to, and divorced from, [[Susan Eisenhower]], granddaughter of [[Dwight D. Eisenhower]].<ref name="samford.edu">{{cite web |url=http://www.samford.edu/schools/artsci/comarts/davislecture/Eisenhower2002.htm |title=Davis Lecture -- Susan Eisenhower |website=www.samford.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081012004231/http://www.samford.edu/schools/artsci/comarts/davislecture/Eisenhower2002.htm |archive-date=2008-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.susaneisenhower.com/faq/ |title=FAQ {{!}} Susan Eisenhower |website=www.susaneisenhower.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080916084728/http://www.susaneisenhower.com/faq/ |archive-date=2008-09-16}}</ref> Sagdeev was the recipient of the 2003 [[Carl Sagan Memorial Award]], and the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] (2001).

==Early years==
Roald Sagdeev is an ethnic [[Tatars|Tatar]]. His maternal grandfather was a secular man teaching mathematics. He was born in Moscow on December 26, 1932, soon after the arrival of his young parents from [[Tatarstan]]. The family used to speak Russian at home. Nonetheless, the parents also communicated in [[Tatar language|Tatar]] between adults when secrecy was needed. He lived with them until the age of four near the [[Nikitsky Gates]]. His father was then a post-graduate student. He spent the following years in [[Kazan]] where he graduated from high school. The young Roald was not only a quite outstanding student who was awarded the silver medal but he was also a chess champion among juniors of his city. His brother Renad Zinnurovich Sagdeev (born December 13, 1941) would later study chemistry. Roald returned to Moscow to study at the [[Moscow State University]]. He was one of the Nobel laureate [[Lev Landau]]'s few students. In the dormitory, he lived next to [[Mikhail Gorbachev]], a law student, and [[Raisa Gorbacheva]], a sociology student.

==As a researcher==
In 1955, after graduating from [[Moscow State University]] in [[Nuclear physics|nuclear science]], with  a doctorate in physics and mathematics, he worked at the [[Kurchatov Institute|Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy]] as a member of the controlled fusion team, with [[Igor Kurchatov]] as director from 1956 to 1961. From 1961 until 1970, he worked as head of the Laboratory at the [[Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics|Institute of Nuclear Physics]] of the Siberian Division of the USSR Academy of Sciences in [[Novosibirsk]].

At the age of 35, he was one of the youngest persons ever elected as a full academician of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.peoples.ru/science/space/sagdeev/|title =Роальд Сагдеев|publisher= ЛЮДИ|date=2004-12-31|accessdate=July 14, 2008}}</ref> From 1970 until 1973, he worked at the Institute of Physics of High Temperatures of the USSR Academy of Sciences. 
==Director of the Space Research Institute==
Upon his return to Moscow, he was appointed the director of the [[Russian Space Research Institute|Space Research Institute of the USSR Academy of Sciences]]. He stayed at this post from 1973 until 1988. There he supervised several research projects such as the [[Kosmos (satellite)|Kosmos]], Forecast, [[Interkosmos]], [[Meteor (satellite)|Meteor]], and [[Astron (spacecraft)|Astron]] programs.

He managed or was a principal participant in many space projects including the [[Venera]] probes to Venus, the joint Soviet-U.S. Soyuz Apollo Test Project and headed the International Space Project [[Venus-Halley]] ([[Vega]]) and [[Phobos program|Phobos]] projects.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.space.com/missionlaunches/missions/sagdeev_interview_010625-1.html|title=Roald Sagdeev: Russia Not Ready for Prime Time|publisher=[[Space.com]]|date=2001-06-26|accessdate=July 13, 2008|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015235802/http://www.space.com/missionlaunches/missions/sagdeev_interview_010625-1.html|archivedate=October 15, 2008}}</ref>

He is the author of studies on [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and [[magnetohydrodynamics|magnetofluiddynamics]]. In 1984, he was awarded the most prestigious [[Lenin Prize]] for his outstanding achievements in the foundations of the neoclassical theory of transport processes in [[Zonal flow (plasma)|toroidal plasma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tatar.ru/?DNSID=1fd37f3cc6c1c7c77f81a3d1a4eec492&node_id=1175&id=1934|title=Сагдеев Роальд Зиннурович|publisher=Департамент внешних связей Президента Республики Татарстан|date=2008-07-15|accessdate=July 15, 2008|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080717074149/http://www.tatar.ru/?DNSID=498bff99427602b06e8827da2bac8e1a|archivedate=July 17, 2008}}</ref>

==Role in politics==
As [[Yuri Andropov]] became the new [[General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union]], Sagdeev participated in the work of a think tank with Gorbachev as the head, which was mandated to find scientific justifications for [[nuclear disarmament]]. Later, as Gorbachev became the new General Secretary, following [[Ronald Reagan]]'s [[Strategic Defense Initiative]] (SDI), they advised the Soviet leadership not to worry and not to respond by creating a similar program.

He was awarded the title of [[Hero of Socialist Labour]] for his role in the international research programme of the Halley Comet in 1986.

He was elected to the [[Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union]] in 1987 and worked until 1991 as an advisor on the issues related to civil and military space problems for [[Mikhail Gorbachev]] and [[Eduard Shevardnadze]] on summits, which were held [[Geneva Summit (1985)|in Geneva]] (1985), [[Washington Summit (1987)|in Washington, D.C.]] (1987) and [[Moscow Summit (1988)|in Moscow]] (1988). However, following the Moscow Summit, Sagdeev was removed from a state visit to Poland in July 1988 and felt "excommunicated" from Soviet leadership after writing a letter criticizing the slowness of the Soviet [[supercomputer]] program.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andersen |first=Ross |date=2025-07-31 |title=Every Scientific Empire Comes to an End |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2025/07/science-empire-america-decline/683711/ |website=The Atlantic |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1987, Sagdeev met [[Susan Eisenhower]] at a US-USSR forum in New York City. Eisenhower, a political scientist and granddaughter of [[Dwight D. Eisenhower]], married Sagdeev in 1990. Following the marriage, Sagdeev relocated to the United States. The couple divorced in 2008.<ref name="samford.edu"/>

In 2024, Sagdeev married Elena Popova, an astrophysicist from Moscow whom he had met at academic conferences in [[Baku]]. Popova is also a composer.<ref name="w_s9kqvowUY">{{cite web |title=Roald Sagdeev and Elena Popova – Science and Personal Life |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w_s9kqvowUY |website=YouTube |publisher=RASA |date=2024-12-10 |access-date=2024-12-13 |language=ru}}</ref>

==Post-Cold War==
Sagdeev is a Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], member of the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine|US National Academy]] and the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]. He is also a member of the Supervisory Council of the [[International Luxembourg Forum on Preventing Nuclear Catastrophe]]. He is a senior advisor at the [[Albright Stonebridge Group]], a global strategy firm, where he assists clients with issues involving Russia and countries of the former Soviet Union.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.albrightstonebridge.com/team/roald-sagdeev/|title=Albright Stonebridge Group|accessdate=September 1, 2019}}</ref>
